title: Paul Tudor Jones: Regulate AI Now or Pay Later
excerpt: The legendary macro investor calls the AI bull market a ticking clock — and demands mandatory deepfake watermarking before it's too late.
body:
Billionaire hedge fund manager Paul Tudor Jones delivered a stark double warning on May 7, 2026: the U.S. government is dangerously late on AI regulation, and the AI-fueled stock market rally looks exactly like 1999 — right before the crash.

**What Jones said:**
Speaking on CNBC's 'Squawk Box,' Jones argued that governments must watermark AI-generated content to distinguish it from deepfakes, calling mandatory watermarking 'the single most transformative thing' policymakers could do. He has personally encountered deepfakes twice in the past year — each time, 'very serious people' called him to ask if he had seen certain content that turned out to be fabricated. His proposed enforcement: make knowing violations a felony, punishable by jail time.

**The market bubble warning:**
Jones sees the AI bull market continuing for another one to two years, but the endgame concerns him deeply. U.S. stock valuations already sit at 252% of GDP. If equities climb a further 40%, that ratio could hit 300–350% — a level Jones says would set up a 30–35% correction of breathtaking severity. He draws the parallel to 1999 deliberately: not to endorse the rally, but to flag what always follows. He is still buying AI stocks, calculating that the final leg of a bubble can be its most profitable — while making clear the exit will be painful.

**What to watch:**
Congress has yet to pass any federal AI regulation framework, and Jones's call for U.S.-China dialogue on AI safety will test whether Washington treats this as the macro risk event it is.
